messages.content: Our API started returning 5xx at 14:02. We deployed v3.14.2 at 13:58. What is the most likely cause and what should we do?
Most likely the deploy: the errors began four minutes after v3.14.2 went out. The fastest safe move is to roll back to v3.14.1, then diff the two releases once things are stable.
We rolled back at 14:20 and the errors are still there. The database connection pool shows 498 of 500 in use.

Then the deploy is not the cause: the errors survived the rollback. A pool at 498/500 means requests are queuing for connections. Look for sessions holding many connections, such as a long-running query or a leak, and list the longest-running ones.
Found it: a report query was holding about 300 connections. We killed it at 14:41 and the errors went to zero at 14:43. Give me an update, based only on what I just told you.

required_facts: The earlier suspicion that the v3.14.2 deploy caused the outage was wrong: the root cause is the report query holding about 300 connections
Recovery: after killing the query at 14:41, errors dropped to zero at 14:43 (as the user reported)
The service is still running v3.14.1 after the rollback, which turned out to be unnecessary, so a decision is needed about rolling forward again
Why the report query ran and how to prevent a repeat are not known yet
critical_omissions: Still attributing the outage to the deploy
Claiming the recurrence is prevented or that the full root cause (why the query ran) is known
Omitting that the earlier deploy hypothesis was withdrawn
unnecessary_repetition: The timeline of the deploy at 13:58 and the first errors at 14:02
The explanation of why a pool at 498/500 causes queuing
The earlier advice to diff the two releases
